old: Here is the complete local/global obstruction check. Use the constant-module squaring sequence 1 \(\to \) \(\{\pm 1\}\) \(\to \) \(\mu _{\infty }\) \(\to \) \(\mu _{\infty }\) \(\to \) 1. By local reciprocity, a finite character of \(G_{Qp}\) has a character square root exactly when its character on Qp* does. The torsion factor of Qp* is cyclic of even order; its only obstruction is the value at -1. The valuation \(Z\) factor admits a finite-order square root. For odd \(p\), squaring on the pro-p principal units is an automorphism; for \(p=2\) the torsion-free factor \(1+4Z_{2}\) is procyclic and its generator's image may be given a square root of twice the order. Thus the criterion holds also at 2, with no omitted principal-unit obstruction. Local \(H^{2}(G_{Qp},\{\pm 1\})\) has two elements, by Kummer and the local Brauer invariant. The boundary of \(\chi \) equals the sign class at every finite prime. The latter is zero outside \(T\) because its class inflates from the unramified local quotient, which has cohomological dimension one. The global Brauer injection and invariant-sum exact sequence determine the real invariant as well. See the final Milne ADT second edition, I.1.3/I.1.6(b,c), and the proof of II.2.1, printed 164, for the reciprocity and Brauer statements.

old: A continuous pointwise square root \(b_{0}\) of \(\chi \) has values in \(\mu _{2m}\). Equality of cohomology classes means \(\delta (b_{0})/\epsilon _{\text{sign}}\) is the coboundary of a continuous sign cochain; correcting \(b_{0}\) supplies \(b^{2}=\chi \) and \(\delta \) \(b=\epsilon _{\text{sign}}\). Normalize \(b(1)=1\). On \(G_{L}\), the cocycle is 1, so \(b\) is a character. For \(h\) in \(G_{L}\) and \(g\) in \(G_{Q}\), the identities \(\epsilon _{\text{sign}}(g,h)=\epsilon _{\text{sign}}(h,g)=1\) show \(b(gh)=b(g)b(h)=b(h)b(g)\), and then \(b(\text{ghg}^{-1})=b(h)\). Its kernel in \(G_{L}\) is therefore normal in \(G_{Q}\).

old: To obtain a Dirichlet twist one may use the inherited Washington Theorem14.1; its final page was not reacquired here. The following replacement uses the final published Milne ADT already inspected: I.1.3 and1.6(c), pp.18--19, give global reciprocity for the idele class group, compatible with the local maps. Composing the finite character \(\delta \) with reciprocity gives a finite continuous idele-class character. The connected positive real component acts trivially. Every rational idele class has a representative whose finite components lie in product \(Z_{p}*\), unique after choosing positive real component; this follows by multiplying by the rational product of its finite uniformizer powers. A finite continuous character of that compact product factors through (Z/rZ)\emph{ for some \(r\). Write \(\lambda \) for this idele-class character. In the decomposition \(C_{Q}=R_{>}0\) times product \(Z_{p}\)}, the idele which is a uniformizer \(q\) at \(q\) and1 elsewhere is represented, after multiplication by \(q^{-1}\), by positive real component1/q and finite units \(q^{-1}\) at every \(p\ne q\) and1 at \(q\). Therefore, with arithmetic reciprocity, define \(\eta \) on (Z/rZ)* to be the inverse of \(\lambda \) restricted to the finite units; then \(\eta (q)=\delta (\text{Frob}_{q})\) for \(q\) prime to \(r\). If the published reciprocity convention is inverse arithmetic, invert that reciprocity map first. This retains the necessary inverse on the finite-unit character rather than silently reversing the twist. This derivation uses neither Washington's unreacquired page nor an unpublished theorem.

old: dominating \(\Gamma \). Blowing up a closed regular point of a regular surface is regular: for regular parameters u,v its charts are T[v/u] and T[u/v], and at an exceptional point \(u\) and a lift of a uniformizer of the local ring of \(P1_{\kappa (x)}\) form regular parameters. This also covers non-rational closed centres. The resulting \(Z\) is integral, proper over \(R\) and R-flat (its coordinate rings have no R-torsion); the generic fibre is \(X\), because every centre lies over a finite prime. Indeed \(\Gamma \to M\) was already an isomorphism on the entire generic fibre. The two maps are \(\alpha :Z\to M\) and \(\beta :Z\to Y\), both proper birational, with identity on \(X\).

\paragraph{Operative primitive-form supplier for this receiving revision.}
For the current $214$ application, the existence assertion in the next
historical Li attribution is supplied instead by the explicit
Deligne--Serre extraction in Part~I, M3
(Section~\ref{q214:modularity}), using \cite[\S\S1.6--1.9, pp.~509--510]{deligne-serre1974}.
The nonzero cusp eigenform $h$ has a nonzero primitive constituent;
good-prime Hecke operators commute with its oldform degeneracy maps,
and uniqueness of that decomposition passes the same eigenvalues to it.
Normalize its first coefficient to $1$. Here the twisting character is
primitive of conductor $r$ as chosen above; in the Part~I Milne route,
take $r=\operatorname{cond}(\eta)$, the least modulus, with the same
Galois character and controlled field. The application is bound explicitly
in \nolinkurl{research/quartic214-protocol-d-progress/CURRENT_NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_APPLICATION.json}.
Li's uniqueness and Fricke uses remain separate. The following original
wording is retained as historical source evidence, qualified by this
operative supplier; no existence claim rests on Li's Theorem~5 alone.
